reviewNotes: S10 accuracy fixes, item 4. Body language: en. Only the listed spans change.

24i9nfn2c.before: To give you a better understanding of AI token pricing, let's consider an example. Suppose you're using a language model to translate 1,000 words from English to Spanish. The provider might charge $0.001 per word for this service. If the model requires 10 tokens per word, your total cost would be 10 x $0.001 = $0.01.
24i9nfn2c.after: To give you a better understanding of AI token pricing, let's consider an example. Suppose you're using a language model to translate 1,000 words from English to Spanish. The provider might charge $10 per 1 million tokens for this service. English text averages about 1.3 tokens per word, so the 1,000 words you send come to about 1,300 input tokens, costing about 1,300 x $10 / 1,000,000 = $0.013. The translated text you get back is billed as output tokens on top of that.
24i9nfn2c.reason: Mixes a per-word price with tokens, "10 tokens per word" is ~8x too high (OpenAI: 100 tokens ≈ 75 words), and "10 x $0.001" prices 10 tokens, not 1,000 words. Illustrative per-token rate, OpenAI's published rule of thumb, arithmetic shown; output tokens noted.
